verses.32:28: And Moses appointed for them Eleazar the priest, and Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel,
verses.32:29: and Moses said to them, "If the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad cross over the Jordan with you, every man armed for war before the Lord, and you subdue the land before you, then you shall give to them the land of Gilead as a possession;
verses.32:30: but if they do not cross over armed with you for the war before the Lord, bring their dependents, their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan, and they will be allotted an inheritance together among you in the land of Canaan."
verses.32:31: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad answered, saying, "Whatever our lord says to his attendants, so we will do;
verses.32:32: we will cross over armed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and you will give the possession to us across the Jordan."
verses.32:33: And Moses gave to them, to the sons of Gad, to the sons of Reuben, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh of the sons of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land and the cities with its borders, the cities of the land all around.
verses.32:34: And the sons of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer,
verses.32:35: and Sophar and Jazer, and they raised them up;
verses.32:36: and Namram and Beth-haran, fortified cities, and sheepfolds.
verses.32:37: And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim,
verses.32:38: and Baal-meon, encircled, and Sibmah; and they named the names of the cities which they built according to their own names.
verses.32:39: And a son of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and took it, and destroyed the Amorite who dwelt in it.
verses.32:40: And Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he dwelt there.
verses.32:41: And Jair the son of Manasseh went and took their settlements, and named them Settlements of Jair.
verses.32:42: And Nabau went and took Kaath and its villages, and named them Naboth after his own name.
verses.33:1: And these are the stopping places of the sons of Israel, as they went out from the land of Egypt with their force by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
verses.33:2: And Moses wrote down their departures and their stopping places by the word of the Lord. And these are the stopping places of their journey.
verses.33:3: They departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the day after the Passover the sons of Israel went out with a high hand before all the Egyptians.
verses.33:4: And the Egyptians were burying all of their own who had died, whom the Lord had struck, every firstborn in the land of Egypt; and on their gods the Lord executed vengeance.
verses.33:5: And having departed from Rameses, the sons of Israel encamped at Succoth.
verses.33:6: And they departed from Succoth and encamped at Buthan, which is part of the wilderness.
verses.33:7: And they departed from Buthan and encamped at the mouth of Epiroth, which is opposite Baal-zephon, and they encamped opposite Migdol.
verses.33:8: And they departed from opposite Hiroth and crossed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness; and they traveled a journey of three days through the wilderness and encamped at Bitterness.
verses.33:9: And they departed from Bitterness and came to Elim; and at Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy trunks of palm trees; and they encamped there beside the water.
verses.33:10: And they departed from Elim and encamped by the Red Sea.
verses.33:11: And they departed from the Red Sea and encamped in the wilderness of Sin.
verses.33:12: And they departed from the wilderness of Sin and encamped at Raphaka.
verses.33:13: And they departed from Raphaka and encamped at Elim.
verses.33:14: And they departed from Elim and encamped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink there.
verses.33:15: And they departed from Rephidim and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.33:16: And they departed from the wilderness of Sinai and encamped at Graves of Craving.
verses.33:17: And they departed from Graves of Craving and encamped at Hazeroth.
verses.33:18: And they departed from Hazeroth and encamped at Rithmah.
verses.33:19: And they departed from Rithmah and encamped at Rimmon-perez.
verses.33:20: And they departed from Rimmon-perez and encamped at Lemona.
verses.33:21: And they departed from Lemona and encamped at Dessa.
verses.33:22: And they departed from Dessa and encamped at Makellath.
verses.33:23: And they departed from Makellath and encamped at Shepher.
verses.33:24: And they departed from Shepher and encamped at Haradah.
verses.33:25: And they departed from Haradah and encamped at Makheloth.
verses.33:26: And they departed from Makheloth and encamped at Kataath.
verses.33:27: And they departed from Kataath and encamped at Tarath.
verses.33:28: And they departed from Tarath and encamped at Mithkah.
verses.33:29: And they departed from Mithkah and encamped at Zalmonah.
verses.33:30: And they departed from Zalmonah and encamped at Moseroth.
verses.33:31: And they departed from Moseroth and encamped at Banaia.
verses.33:32: And they departed from Banaia and encamped at Mount Gadgad.
verses.33:33: And they departed from Mount Gadgad and encamped at Setebatha.
verses.33:34: And they departed from Setebatha and encamped at Sebrona.
verses.33:35: And they departed from Sebrona and encamped at Ezion-geber.
verses.33:36: And they departed from Ezion-geber and encamped in the wilderness of Zin; and they departed from the wilderness of Zin and encamped in the wilderness of Paran, that is, Kadesh.
verses.33:37: And they departed from Kadesh and encamped at Mount Hor, near the land of Edom.
verses.33:38: And Aaron the priest went up by the command of the Lord and died there in the fortieth year of the exodus of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first of the month.
verses.33:39: And Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
verses.33:40: And the Canaanite, king of Arad, heard—and he was dwelling in the land of Canaan—when the sons of Israel were entering.
verses.33:41: And they departed from Mount Hor and encamped at Zalmonah.
verses.33:42: And they departed from Zalmonah and encamped at Punon.
verses.33:43: And they departed from Punon and encamped at Soboth.
verses.33:44: And they departed from Soboth and encamped at Gai, on the other side, at the borders of Moab.
verses.33:45: And they departed from Gai and encamped at Dibon-gad.
verses.33:46: And they departed from Dibon-gad and encamped at Almon-diblathaim.
verses.33:47: And they departed from Almon-diblathaim and encamped on the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
verses.33:48: And they departed from the mountains of Abarim and encamped on the west of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
verses.33:49: And they encamped beside the Jordan between Aesimoth as far as Belsa, which is toward the west of Moab.
verses.33:50: And the Lord spoke to Moses on the west of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho, saying,
verses.33:51: "Speak to the sons of Israel and you shall say to them, 'You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan.
verses.33:52: And you shall destroy all those dwelling in the land before you, and you shall remove their watchtowers, and all their cast idols you shall destroy, and all their pillars you shall remove.
verses.33:53: And you shall destroy all those dwelling in the land and you shall dwell in it, for to you I have given their land as an allotment.
verses.33:54: And you shall inherit their land by lot according to their tribes; to the more numerous you shall increase their possession, and to the fewer you shall decrease their possession; wherever his name comes out there, it shall be his; according to the tribes of your families you shall inherit.
verses.33:55: But if you do not destroy those dwelling on the land from before you, then those of them whom you leave behind will be thorns in your eyes and darts in your sides, and they will be hostile on the land on which you will dwell.
verses.33:56: And it will be that just as I had determined to do to them, I will do to you.'"
verses.34:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:2: "Command the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You are entering the land of Canaan; this shall be for you as the inheritance, the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
verses.34:3: And the side toward the south shall be for you from the wilderness of Zin as far as bordering Edom, and the boundary toward the south shall be for you from the edge of the Salt Sea on the east;
verses.34:4: and the boundary shall turn around you from the south toward the ascent of Akrabbim, and pass by Ennak, and its outlet shall be south of Kadesh-barnea; and it shall go out to the village of Arad, and pass by Azmon.
verses.34:5: And the boundary shall turn around from Azmon to the brook of Egypt, and the outlet shall be the sea.
verses.34:6: And the boundary of the sea shall be for you: the Great Sea shall mark the boundary; this shall be for you the boundary of the sea.
verses.34:7: And this shall be the boundary for you toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure out for yourselves alongside the mountain, the mountain;
verses.34:8: and from the mountain, the mountain you shall measure out for them as they enter Hamath, and their outlet shall be the boundary of Saradak;
verses.34:9: and the boundary shall go out to Dephrona, and its outlet shall be Harsenaim; this shall be a boundary for you on the north.
verses.34:10: And you shall measure out for yourselves the boundary of the east from Harsenain to Sepphamar;
verses.34:11: and the boundary shall go down from Sepphamar to Bela, on the east toward springs; and the boundary of Bela shall go down upon the back of the Sea of Chenara on the east.
verses.34:12: And the boundary shall go down to the Jordan, and the outlet shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be the land for you, and its boundaries all around.'"
verses.34:13: And Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying, "This is the land which you shall inherit by lot, just as the Lord instructed Moses to give it to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe of Manasseh;
verses.34:14: for the tribe of the sons of Reuben and the tribe of the sons of Gad have received theirs according to the houses of their fathers, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their allotments.
verses.34:15: Two tribes and a half-tribe have received their allotments beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, from the south toward the east."
verses.34:16: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:17: "These are the names of the men who shall allot the land to you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.34:18: And you shall take one leader from each tribe to allot the land to you as an inheritance.
verses.34:19: And these are the names of the men: of the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
verses.34:20: of the tribe of Simeon, Salamiel son of Semiud;
verses.34:21: of the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon;
verses.34:22: of the tribe of Dan, a leader, Bakchir son of Egli;
verses.34:23: of the sons of Joseph, of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, a leader, Hanniel son of Suphi;
verses.34:24: of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, a leader, Kemuel son of Sabatha;
verses.34:25: of the tribe of Zebulun, a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
verses.34:26: of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, a leader, Paltiel son of Oza;
verses.34:27: of the tribe of the sons of Asher, a leader, Achior son of Shelomi;
verses.34:28: of the tribe of Naphtali, a leader, Pedahel son of Beniamiud."
verses.34:29: These are the ones whom the Lord commanded to apportion shares to the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan.
verses.35:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses at the west of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying,
verses.35:2: "Instruct the sons of Israel, and they shall give to the Levites from the allotments of their possession cities to live in, and they shall give to the Levites the outskirts of the cities all around them;
verses.35:3: and the cities shall be for them to live in, and their set-apart grounds shall be for their livestock and for all their four-footed animals.
verses.35:4: And the adjoining areas of the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall be from the wall of the city and outward two thousand cubits all around;
verses.35:5: and you shall measure outside the city the side toward the east, two thousand cubits, and the side toward the south, two thousand cubits, and the side toward the sea, two thousand cubits, and the side toward the north, two thousand cubits; and the city in the middle of this shall be for you, and the bordering areas of the cities.
verses.35:6: And you shall give the cities to the Levites: the six cities of refuge which you shall give for the killer to flee there, and in addition to these, forty-two cities;
verses.35:7: you shall give all the cities to the Levites, even forty-eight cities, these and their outskirts.
verses.35:8: And as for the cities which you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel: from those who have many, many, and from those who are fewer, fewer; each according to his inheritance which they shall inherit, they shall give from the cities to the Levites."
verses.35:9: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.35:10: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'You are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.35:11: and you shall set apart cities for yourselves; they shall be places of refuge for you, for the killer to flee there, everyone who strikes down a person unintentionally.
verses.35:12: And the cities shall be places of refuge for you from the kinsman-avenger of blood, and the killer shall certainly not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
verses.35:13: And the cities which you shall give, the six cities, shall be places of refuge for you;
verses.35:14: three cities you shall give beyond the Jordan, and the three cities you shall give in the land of Canaan.
verses.35:15: It shall be a refuge for the sons of Israel, and for the proselyte, the resident alien who is among you; these cities shall be for a place of refuge, for everyone who strikes down a person unintentionally to flee there.
verses.35:16: But if he strikes him with an iron implement and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
verses.35:17: And if he strikes him with a stone from the hand, by which he would die, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death.
verses.35:18: And if he strikes him with a wooden implement from the hand, from which he would die, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must surely be put to death;
verses.35:19: the kinsman-avenger of blood himself shall kill the killer; when he himself meets him, he shall kill him.
verses.35:20: And if out of enmity he pushes him and throws any implement at him from ambush, and he dies,
verses.35:21: or out of wrath he strikes him with his hand, and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death; he is a murderer; the killer must surely be put to death; the kinsman-avenger of blood shall kill the killer when he meets him.
verses.35:22: But if suddenly, not out of enmity, he pushes him or throws any implement at him not from ambush,
verses.35:23: or with any stone by which he would die, without knowing, and it falls upon him, and he dies, though he was not his enemy nor seeking to harm him,
verses.35:24: then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck him and the kinsman-avenger of blood according to these judgments.
verses.35:25: And the congregation shall rescue the killer from the kinsman-avenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to the city of his refuge where he fled for refuge; and he shall live there until the high priest dies, whom they anointed with the holy oil.
verses.35:26: But if the killer ever goes out beyond the boundaries of the city to which he fled for refuge,
verses.35:27: and the kinsman-avenger of blood finds him outside the boundaries of the city of his refuge, and the kinsman-avenger of blood kills the killer, he is not guilty;
verses.35:28: for he must live in the city of refuge until the high priest dies; after the high priest dies, the killer shall return to the land of his possession.
verses.35:29: And these things shall be for you as a statute of judgment throughout your generations in all your dwelling places.
verses.35:30: As for everyone who strikes down a person, by witnesses you shall kill the killer, and one witness shall not testify against a person so that he dies;
verses.35:31: and you shall not take a ransom for the life from the killer who is liable to be executed, for he shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:32: You shall not take a ransom for fleeing to a city of refuge, to live again on the land until the high priest dies.
verses.35:33: And you shall certainly not stain with murder the land in which you live, for this blood stains the land with murder; and the land shall not be atoned for from the blood that was shed upon it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
verses.35:34: And you shall not defile the land upon which you live, upon which I will dwell among you; for I am the Lord who dwells in the midst of the sons of Israel.'"
verses.36:1: And the leaders of the tribe of the sons of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of the sons of Joseph, came forward and spoke before Moses and before Eleazar the priest and before the leaders of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel.
verses.36:2: And they said, "The Lord commanded our lord to assign the land of the inheritance by lot to the sons of Israel, and the Lord ordered our lord to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.
verses.36:3: And they will become wives to one from the tribes of the sons of Israel, and their allotment will be taken away from the possession of our fathers, and it will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to whom they become wives, and from the allotment of our inheritance it will be taken away.
verses.36:4: And if the release of the sons of Israel comes, then their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to whom they become wives, and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our ancestral family."
verses.36:5: And Moses commanded the sons of Israel by the decree of the Lord, saying, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks thus.
verses.36:6: This is the word that the Lord ordered for the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, 'Where it is pleasing in their sight, let them become wives; only to those from the clan of their father let them become wives.
verses.36:7: And an inheritance for the sons of Israel shall not shift from tribe to tribe, for the sons of Israel shall indeed cling, each one to the inheritance of the tribe of his ancestral family.
verses.36:8: And every daughter who succeeds to an inheritance from the tribes of the sons of Israel shall become a wife to one of those from the clan of her father, so that the sons of Israel may each succeed to the ancestral inheritance.
verses.36:9: And an allotment shall not shift from one tribe to another tribe, but the sons of Israel shall cling, each one to his inheritance.'"
verses.36:10: In the manner that the Lord ordered Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.
verses.36:11: And Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, Noah, and Mahlah, the daughters of Zelophehad, were married to their cousins.
verses.36:12: They became wives to those from the clan of Manasseh, of the sons of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of the clan of their father.
verses.36:13: These are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments that the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses at the west of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.

notes.1:4: The Greek syntax ("each man by the tribe of each of the leaders, and they shall be by houses of ancestral families") diverges notably from the Hebrew MT ("one man from each tribe, each being head of his father's house").
notes.1:14: The Greek reads Rhagouel (Reuel), matching Numbers 2:14, whereas the Hebrew MT here reads Deuel.
notes.1:18: The Greek date reads "of the month of the second year" (where the Hebrew MT reads "of the second month"), and the rare verb epexonoysan refers to registering names on official tablets or rolls (axones).
notes.1:33: The Greek gives Manasseh's count as 32,300 (Hebrew MT: 32,200), though the total in v. 46 remains 603,550; the Greek also places Gad at vv. 36-37 after Benjamin rather than at vv. 24-25 before Judah as in MT.
notes.1:53: The Greek adds "before the Lord" and reads "sin" (hamartema) among the sons of Israel, whereas the Hebrew MT reads "wrath" upon the congregation of the sons of Israel.
notes.2:2: The Greek reads 'each man next to him' (anthropos echomenos autou) for the ordered placement of the tribes, and consistently renders 'tent of meeting' as 'the tent of testimony' (he skene tou martyriou).
notes.2:3: The Greek text uniquely reads 'toward the south, toward the east' (kata noton kat' anatolas), where the Hebrew has 'eastward, toward the sunrise.'
notes.2:18: 'By the sea' (para thalassan) is a literal Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew directional idiom for 'westward' (toward the Mediterranean Sea).
notes.2:21: The Greek text reads 'thirty-two thousand four hundred' (tetrakosioi), whereas the Hebrew has 32,200 (which aligns with the division total of 108,100 in 2:24).
notes.2:26: The Greek text reads 'sixty-two thousand five hundred' (pentakosioi), whereas the Hebrew has 62,700 (which aligns with the division total of 157,600 in 2:31).
notes.3:2: The Greek reads Abiud (Ἀβιούδ, also in 3:4), rendered with the standard modern English spelling Abihu throughout Exodus–Numbers.
notes.3:17: The Greek text reads Γεδσών (Gedson, a dalet/resh variation) throughout Numbers, rendered here with the standard modern English spelling Gershon.
notes.3:20: The Greek reads Ὀμουσεί (Omushi, reflecting the Hebrew conjunction u- fused onto the name), rendered with the standard English spelling Mushi to match Exodus 6:19 and the clan name Mushite in 3:33.
notes.3:24: Greek reads Dael (from a delta/lambda or dalet/lamed interchange), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Lael.
notes.3:34: Greek gives the Merarite count as 6,050, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 6,200; in both traditions the sum of the three clans exceeds the stated total of 22,000 in 3:39.
notes.3:47: Greek renders the sanctuary weight standard with Ptolemaic monetary terms ("holy didrachma" and "twenty obols to the shekel"), where the Hebrew reads "shekel of the sanctuary" and "twenty gerahs to the shekel."
notes.4:3: The Greek text consistently sets the starting age for Levitical service at twenty-five (also in vv. 23, 30, 35, 39, 43, and 47), matching Numbers 8:24 rather than the thirty years found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:14: In vv. 13-14 the Greek directs placing "the cover" (καλυπτήρ) on the altar rather than removing its ashes, and adds an instruction absent from the Masoretic Text for wrapping the washbasin and its base in a purple cloth and blue leather covering.
notes.4:22: The Greek text reads Γεδσών (Gedson), the standard Septuagint form of Gershon (also in vv. 24, 27, 28, 38, and 41), rendered here with its standard modern English spelling.
notes.4:26: The Greek reads "the remaining things" (τὰ περισσά), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew root as "remainder" rather than "their cords," and omits the courtyard gate screen present in the Masoretic Text.
notes.4:36: The Greek text gives 2,250 for the Kohathites (whereas the Masoretic Text reads 2,750), while keeping the combined Levitical total of 8,580 in v. 48.
notes.5:2: Greek psyche ("soul") is used in Septuagint purity laws to denote a dead body or corpse (compare 6:6, 11).
notes.5:9: The Greek text has a double dative ("to the Lord, to the priest"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads only "to the priest."
notes.5:17: The Septuagint reads "clean, living water" and "the tent of testimony," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "holy water" and "the tabernacle."
notes.5:18: Greek elegmos ("conviction" or "reproof") reflects a Septuagint rendering distinct from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "bitterness" (similarly in vv. 19, 23, 24, 27).
notes.5:27: Greek lethe lathe ("completely escapes ... notice") echoes v. 13, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "has acted unfaithfully against her husband."
notes.6:2: Throughout this chapter the Septuagint never transliterates "Nazirite," rendering the Hebrew root with terms for vowing (euche) and ritual purity (hagneia, hagnismos).
notes.6:4: The Greek text reads accusative oinon ("wine") in apposition with the grape products rather than a genitive modifier ("vine of wine") as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.6:11: The Septuagint joins the clause "on which he was consecrated to the Lord for the days of the vow" to v. 11 with a passive verb, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text begins v. 12 with an active rededication.
notes.6:14: Greek soterion ("deliverance [offering]") is the Septuagint's standard rendering of the Hebrew peace/fellowship offering (similarly in vv. 17, 18).
notes.6:24: Greek reads 'bless you and guard' without repeating 'you' after 'guard' (supplied in English), and in verse 25 'have mercy on you' (ἐλεήσαι σε).
notes.7:2: The Greek text explicitly counts them as 'twelve leaders,' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads only 'heads of their ancestral houses.'
notes.7:17: Greek 'sacrifice of deliverance' (θυσίαν σωτηρίου) is the Septuagint rendering of the peace or fellowship offering. The Greek also specifies female animals—'two heifers' (δαμάλεις) and 'five year-old ewe lambs' (ἀμνάδας)—where the Hebrew text has oxen and male lambs.
notes.7:29: The Greek text omits 'five he-goats' (τράγους πέντε) from the list here and again in 7:41, likely due to an early scribal skip between repeated instances of 'five.'
notes.7:30: The Greek text reads 'Edisur' (Ἐδισούρ) here, a minor manuscript spelling variant of 'Shedeur' (Σεδιούρ, as in 7:35).
notes.7:42: The Greek text reads 'Reuel' (Ῥαγουήλ), matching Numbers 2:14, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'Deuel' here.
notes.7:84: The Greek reads 'from the sons of Israel' (παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'from the leaders of Israel.'
notes.7:86: The Greek omits the Hebrew clause stating ten shekels per pan by the sanctuary shekel, and gives the total in 'gold pieces' (χρυσοῖ).
notes.7:87: The Greek adds 'and their drink offerings' (καὶ αἱ σπονδαὶ αὐτῶν) after 'their sacrifices,' whereas the Hebrew text mentions only their grain offering.
notes.7:88: The Greek places the sixty ewe lambs before the he-goats and adds 'without blemish' (ἄμωμοι). It also adds 'after filling his hands' (the priestly ordination idiom) and reads masculine 'anointing him' (αὐτόν) rather than neuter 'it' for the altar.
notes.7:89: The Greek explicitly reads 'the voice of the Lord' (τὴν φωνήν Κυρίου), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads simply 'the voice.'
notes.8:8: The Greek reads "year-old" (eniausion) for the second calf, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a second" (sheni).
notes.8:11: Greek apodoma ("gift", also in vv. 13, 16, 19, 21) renders Hebrew terms for both "wave offering" (tenuphah in vv. 11, 13, 21) and "given ones" (netunim in vv. 16, 19), unifying the section around the Levites being handed over as a gift.
notes.8:19: The Greek states that there shall not be among the sons of Israel "anyone approaching the holy things," omitting the Hebrew Masoretic Text's reference to a "plague" when Israel approaches the sanctuary.
notes.8:26: Greek ho adelphos autou ("his brother") stands as the nominative singular subject of "shall serve," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "he shall serve with his brothers."
notes.9:4: The Greek compresses the transition into v. 5 with the participle enarchomenou ("beginning") on the fourteenth day, lacking the Hebrew Masoretic Text's explicit narrative clause "and they observed the Passover in the first [month]."
notes.9:6: "A human corpse" renders the Greek idiom epi psyche anthropou (literally "because of a human soul," also in vv. 7, 10), which mirrors Hebrew nephesh adam in the legal sense of a dead person.
notes.9:18: From here through v. 23, the Greek shifts from past narrative verbs to future verbs ("will encamp," "will set out"), rendering Hebrew habitual imperfects prospectively; this verse also places "encamp" before "set out," reversing the Hebrew order.
notes.9:22: The Greek lacks the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "two days" and its closing clause ("when it lifted, they set out"); "For a month, for days" translates menos, hemeras, which could also be read as "for a month, for a day."
notes.9:23: The Greek reads "For by the command of the Lord they will set out" without the Hebrew's "they encamped," followed by the appositional relative clause "the watch of the Lord which they kept."
notes.10:6: The Greek includes third and fourth trumpet signals for the camps by the sea (west) and toward the north, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text mentions only the first two signals (east and south).
notes.10:17: Here and in vv. 21, 22, and 25, the Greek shifts from past aorist verbs (vv. 14, 18, 28) to future verbs ("will take down," "will set out," "will set up"), reflecting a prescriptive or habitual rendering of Hebrew weqatal forms.
notes.10:20: The Greek reads "Reuel" (Ragouel) as the father of Eliasaph (matching MT Num 2:14), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text here reads "Deuel."
notes.10:31: The Greek reads "because you were with us in the wilderness, and you will be an elder among us," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "because you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you will serve as eyes for us."
notes.10:34: Verses 34-36 follow the Septuagint verse order, placing Moses's words at the ark's departure and resting (vv. 34-35; MT vv. 35-36) before the notice of the overshadowing cloud (v. 36; MT v. 34). In v. 35, Greek "thousands, ten thousands" (chiliadas myriadas) stands in the accusative without a preposition.
notes.11:3: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Taberah by its meaning as Enpyrismos ("Burning"); similarly, in vv. 34-35 it translates Kibroth-hattaavah as Mnemata tes epithymias ("Graves of Craving").
notes.11:11: Greek horme literally means "impulse," "impetus," or "onrush" (also in v. 17), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "burden."
notes.11:20: Greek cholera denotes an acute bilious sickness accompanied by violent vomiting and nausea, rendering Hebrew "a loathsome thing."
notes.11:28: Greek ho eklektos ("the chosen one") reflects a reading of the Hebrew root for "chosen," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from his youth."
notes.11:32: The Greek renders the dry measure as "kors" (korous; MT "homers") and reads "they slaughtered drying heaps" (esphaxan ... psygmous) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "they spread them out."
notes.12:1: The Greek text reads Aithiopissa ("Ethiopian woman"), rendering the Hebrew "Cushite woman" with the Septuagint's standard geographic equivalent.
notes.12:4: The Greek text uses skene tou martyriou ("tent of testimony") rather than the Hebrew "tent of meeting," and lists Miriam before Aaron.
notes.12:6: The Greek text reads Kyrio ("for the Lord") in the dative and en hypno ("in sleep") rather than "in a dream," resolving a difficult Hebrew clause; in v. 8 it likewise reads "the glory of the Lord" where Hebrew has "the form of the Lord."
notes.12:15: The Greek text reads ekatharisthe ("was cleansed"), whereas the Hebrew text reads "was brought back in."
notes.13:4: Several names in the Septuagint scout list (vv. 4-15) differ genuinely from the Hebrew text: Samuel (v. 4, Heb. Shammua), Suri (v. 5, Heb. Hori), Ilaal (v. 7, Heb. Igal), Naue (vv. 8, 16, Heb. Nun), Gudiel (vv. 10, 15, Heb. Gaddiel and Geuel), Gamai (v. 12, Heb. Gemalli), and Jabi (v. 14, Heb. Vophsi).
notes.13:21: The Greek text reads Rhaab ("Rahab") and Hephaath ("Hephaath") where the Hebrew text reads "Rehob" and "Hamath" (Lebo-hamath).
notes.13:22: The Greek text reads Thelamin (Heb. Talmai) and uses the Greek name Tanin ("Tanis") for the Egyptian city called "Zoan" in the Hebrew text.
notes.13:23: The Greek text translates the place name Eshcol literally as Pharanx botryos ("Valley of the Cluster," vv. 23-24), adds "and scouted it out," and reads sikyon ("cucumbers") instead of sykon ("figs," as in Hebrew).
notes.13:29: The Greek text includes "the Hivite" among the hill-country inhabitants and omits "and along the Jordan" at the end of the verse; in v. 32 it reads ekstasin ("dismay") rather than "bad report," and in v. 33 repeats "before them" twice without "in our own sight."
notes.14:9: The Greek reads "the opportunity" (ὁ καιρός, also "season" or "favorable time"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "their shadow" (i.e., protection).
notes.14:18: Greek katharismo ou kathariei literally reads "with cleansing He will not cleanse," a forensic idiom for "will by no means clear/acquit" (compare Exod 20:7; 34:7; Deut 5:11).
notes.14:23: The Greek includes the extended promise granting the land to the children who do not yet know good or evil (paralleling Deuteronomy 1:39), a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text here.
notes.14:27: The Greek reads "about you" (περὶ ὑμῶν, addressed to Moses and Aaron), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "against Me."
notes.14:33: The Greek middle/passive participle νεμόμενοι ("pasturing" or "grazing") portrays the next generation subsisting in the wilderness like a flock, where the Hebrew has "shepherds."
notes.14:45: The Greek renders Hormah as Ἑρμάν (Herman) and concludes with the clause "and they turned back to the camp," which is not in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:3: The phrase "to magnify a vow" (also in 15:8) translates the Greek literally, reflecting a distinctive Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew idiom for making or fulfilling a special vow.
notes.15:10: The Greek text omits the prescription of half a hin of wine for a drink offering found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, likely through an early scribal omission after "half of a hin" at the end of v. 9.
notes.15:14: The Greek text places "the congregation" at the end of v. 14 as the subject of the final clause ("so the congregation shall do to the Lord"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text places "the assembly" at the beginning of v. 15.
notes.15:30: "With a hand of arrogance" is a literal rendering of the Greek idiom for defiant or presumptuous action; the Greek also reads "provokes God" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "blasphemes the Lord."
notes.15:39: Following the Greek verse division, "so that you may remember and do all My commandments" concludes v. 39 rather than opening v. 40 as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, and "it shall be for you in the tassels" refers to the blue cord placed in them.
notes.16:1: The Greek reads "spoke" (elalesen) rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "took," which lacks an explicit object in Hebrew.
notes.16:5: The Greek reads "God has examined" (epeskeptai) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "in the morning" (boqer), reflecting a verbal reading of the same Hebrew consonants.
notes.16:13: The Greek text reads "into a land" (eis gen) rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "out of a land," and verse 14 continues as a contrafactual conditional ("Even if you had brought us... you would have gouged out").
notes.16:15: The Greek reads "desirable thing" (epithymema) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "donkey" (chamor), reflecting a single-consonant difference in the underlying Hebrew.
notes.16:26: The Greek text reads "these harsh men" (skleron) and "with all your belongings" (en pase te apartia hymon); the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "wicked" and "in all their sins," and some Greek manuscripts read hamartia auton ("their sin").
notes.17:1: In Septuagint versification, chapter 17 begins here (corresponding to 16:36 in Hebrew Bibles), and the Lord addresses both Moses and Eleazar directly rather than telling Moses to speak to Eleazar.
notes.17:7: The Greek reads "rushed" (hormesan) rather than the Hebrew "turned," and renders the Hebrew exclamation with the deictic pronoun "this one" (tende), referring to the tent.
notes.17:11: The Greek text has the third-person singular future "it will make atonement" (exilasetai, referring to the incense) rather than an imperative addressed to Aaron, and uses the verb "shatter" (thrauein, cognate with thrausis, "plague," in verses 12-15).
notes.17:23: The Greek reads "nuts" (karya) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text specifies "almonds," and includes Aaron alongside Moses entering the tent.
notes.18:1: The Greek reads "shall receive the firstfruits of the holy things," differing from the Hebrew MT ("bear the iniquity of the sanctuary"), while using the same verb ("receive/bear") in the second clause for "bear the sins of your priesthood."
notes.18:11: Greek epithemata literally means "things laid on" ("laid-on offerings"), rendering the Hebrew wave offering; the same term recurs in 18:18 alongside "right shoulder" (brachion, where the Hebrew MT has "thigh").
notes.18:16: The Greek uses "obols" (oboloi), a Greek unit of weight and coinage, as the equivalent of the Hebrew gerah (one-twentieth of a holy shekel).
notes.18:19: Greek aphairema ("contribution") literally means a portion taken off or set aside; "a covenant of eternal salt" preserves the Greek genitive agreement (halos aioniou), denoting an enduring salt-ratified covenant.
notes.18:28: The Greek includes a difficult masculine plural pronoun ("set them aside from the contributions of the Lord"), likely an early textual variation within the Greek tradition where the Hebrew MT reads "you also shall present a contribution to the Lord."
notes.19:3: The Greek adds "to a clean place" (absent in the Hebrew MT here, though present in 19:9) and uses plural verbs ("they shall lead... they shall slaughter") for the actions carried out before Eleazar.
notes.19:9: Greek "water of sprinkling" (hydor rantismou) and "purification" (hagnisma) correspond to Hebrew expressions commonly rendered "water for impurity" and "sin offering," highlighting the rite's cleansing function.
notes.19:14: The Greek renders the dwelling as "house" (oikia here and oikos in 19:18) rather than "tent" as in the Hebrew MT, adapting the law to settled domestic contexts.
notes.19:16: Greek traumatias ("one killed" or "fatally wounded") corresponds to the Hebrew phrase for one killed by a sword, without mentioning a sword.
notes.19:19: The Greek reads "he shall be unclean until evening" (matching the phrasing of vv. 7, 8, 10, 21, and 22), whereas the Hebrew MT states positively "he shall be clean at evening."
notes.20:12: The Greek reads "you did not believe so as to sanctify Me," omitting "in Me" (present in the Hebrew) and taking the infinitive directly as the complement of the verb.
notes.20:13: The Septuagint translates Hebrew Meribah here as "water of dispute" (antilogia) and in 20:24 as "water of quarreling" (loidoria), highlighting Israel's verbal contention.
notes.20:19: Where the Hebrew reads "by the highway" and "on foot," the Greek twice reads "along the mountain" (para to oros).
notes.20:24: The Greek uses the second-person plural ("you shall certainly not enter") addressing both Moses and Aaron, and reads "you provoked Me" rather than the Hebrew "you rebelled against My word."
notes.21:3: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew place name Hormah into Greek as Anathema ("devoted to destruction" or "accursed"), preserving the wordplay with the preceding verb.
notes.21:11: Greek "Chalgai on the far side" (Chalgai ek tou peran) is a distinct Septuagint form corresponding to Hebrew Iye-abarim.
notes.21:14: In this citation of the singular "War of the Lord" (Hebrew "Wars of the Lord"), the Greek reads the verb "He set ablaze" with the distinct place name Zoob, where the Hebrew has the obscure phrase "Waheb in Suphah."
notes.21:19: This verse gives the whole itinerary and preserves the distinct Greek forms Manthanain (Hebrew Mattanah), Manael (Hebrew Nahaliel), and Ianen (a proper name where the Hebrew has 'the valley'), and reads 'the hewn rock' (τοῦ λελαξευμένου) where the Hebrew has Pisgah.
notes.21:24: The Septuagint reads the place name "Jazer" where the Hebrew reads "strong" ("for the border of the sons of Ammon was strong").
notes.21:30: The Greek diverges markedly from the Hebrew ("we have shot at them... to Nophah, which reaches to Medeba"), reading "their seed will perish" and "the women still further kindled fire upon Moab."
notes.22:1: The Greek text reads "on the west of Moab" (epi dysmōn Mōab), reflecting the Hebrew consonantal root for "west/evening" rather than the Masoretic Text's "plains of Moab."
notes.22:25: Unlike the Masoretic Text ("she pressed herself against the wall"), the Greek text uses the masculine pronoun auton ("him"), indicating that the donkey pressed Balaam himself against the wall.
notes.22:30: The Greek text reads "from your youth" (apo neotētos sou) and "in utter disregard" (hyperorasei hyperidousa), where the Masoretic Text has "all your life" and "been in the habit of."
notes.22:39: Greek Poleis epauleōn ("Cities of Villages") translates the Hebrew place name Kiriath-huzoth literally rather than transliterating it.
notes.22:41: The Greek text reads "the pillar of Baal" (tēn stēlēn tou Baal) and "he showed him" (edeixen autō), where the Masoretic Text has "Bamoth-baal" ("high places of Baal") and "he saw."
notes.23:7: Greek parabolē ("parable") here denotes an elevated poetic oracle, and "Mesopotamia" reflects the Greek reading Ek Mesopotamias (MT: "from Aram").
notes.23:10: The Greek text differs notably from the Masoretic Text, reading "seed" (sperma, MT: "dust"), "clans" (dēmous, MT: "fourth part"), "among the souls of the righteous" (en psychais dikaiōn), and "my seed" (to sperma mou, MT: "my end").
notes.23:14: The Greek text translates both Hebrew place names literally: agrou skopian ("a field's lookout," MT: "field of Zophim") and Lelaxeumenou ("the Hewn Place," a participle rendering Hebrew "Pisgah").
notes.23:19: The Greek text uses passive infinitives—diartēthēnai ("to be misled / kept in suspense") and apeilēthēnai ("to be threatened")—where the Masoretic Text reads "that he should lie" and "that he should repent."
notes.23:22: Greek monokerōs ("unicorn," literally "one-horned animal") is the Septuagint's standard rendering of Hebrew re'em (probably the wild ox), and doxa ("glory") renders a rare Hebrew noun denoting strength or horns.
notes.24:7: The Greek reads "A man will come forth from his seed" and names "Gog" (where the Hebrew MT reads "water shall flow from his buckets" and "Agag"). Because the Greek lacks "his" on the first "kingdom," the clause may also be read "he will be exalted higher than the kingdom of Gog."
notes.24:8: Greek monokeros ("unicorn," literally "one-horned") renders Hebrew re'em ("wild ox"), and pache ("fat parts") renders Hebrew atzmot ("bones").
notes.24:17: The Greek renders "a man" (for MT "a scepter") and "the leaders of Moab" (for MT "the forehead/corners of Moab"), and opens with "I will show to him" and "I pronounce blessed" (for MT "I see him" and "I behold him"). In 24:18, the Greek also names "Esau" where the Hebrew MT has "Seir."
notes.24:22: Where the Hebrew MT reads "Kain will be consumed" (leba'er Qayin), the Greek reads the proper name "Beor" (le-Beor) and "nest" (qen), rendering "a nest of craftiness" for Beor.
notes.24:23: The Greek adds "and seeing Og" (absent from the Hebrew MT), and in 24:24 renders "the Hebrews" (for MT "Eber") without "ships" before "from the hand of the Kittim."
notes.25:1: Greek ebebelothe ("were profaned") reflects reading the Hebrew root chalal as "profane" rather than "begin" (MT "the people began").
notes.25:6: The Greek reverses the objects relative to the Hebrew MT ("brought the Midianite woman to his brothers"), reading "brought his brother to the Midianite woman."
notes.25:8: Greek kaminon literally means "furnace" or "oven," rendering Hebrew qubbah (a domed tent or vaulted alcove); metras specifically means "womb."
notes.25:14: The Greek gives the father's name as "Salmon," whereas the Hebrew MT reads "Salu."
notes.25:15: The Greek both translates Hebrew ummoth ("peoples/tribes") as "nation" and transliterates it as the proper name "Ommoth."
notes.26:3: Greek transliterates the Hebrew term for "plains" as the place name "Araboth" (Araboth of Moab).
notes.26:4: The Greek text preserves an elliptical command containing the second-person pronoun "you" ("you and the sons of Israel who came out of Egypt"), differing from the Hebrew.
notes.26:10: Greek reads "in his congregation" where the Hebrew has "when that company died," and reads simply "the two hundred and fifty" without "men."
notes.26:15: In vv. 15-31 the Septuagint orders the tribes as Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Gad, and Asher, differing from the Hebrew order (where Gad appears at vv. 15-18 and Asher at vv. 44-47).
notes.26:17: Greek reads the distinct name Jamun (and Jamunites), corresponding to Hebrew Hamul (and Hamulites).
notes.26:22: Greek reads the distinct name Allel (and Allelites), corresponding to Hebrew Jahleel (and Jahleelites).
notes.26:25: Greek reads the distinct name Addi (and Addites), corresponding to Hebrew Eri (and Erites).
notes.26:26: Greek reads Arodi (as in Gen 46:16) and the distinct name Ariel (and Arielites), corresponding to Hebrew Arod and Areli.
notes.26:27: Greek gives Gad's census total as 44,500, whereas the Hebrew reads 40,500.
notes.26:28: Greek reads the distinct name Jamin (and Jaminites) for Asher's first son, corresponding to Hebrew Imnah (and Imnites).
notes.26:29: Greek omits "of the sons of Beriah" before Heber and reads the distinct name Melliel (and Mellielites), corresponding to Hebrew Malchiel.
notes.26:30: Greek reads the distinct name Kara (likely from scribal confusion of uncial sigma and kappa for Sara), corresponding to Hebrew Serah.
notes.26:31: Greek gives Asher's census total as 43,600 (using the Greek alphabetic numeral chi for 600), whereas the Hebrew reads 53,400.
notes.26:34: Greek reads the distinct name Ahiezer (and Ahiezerites), corresponding to Hebrew Iezer (and Iezerites).
notes.26:36: Greek reads the distinct name Symaer (and Symaerites), corresponding to Hebrew Shemida (and Shemidaites).
notes.26:39: Greek omits Becher (present in the Hebrew) and reads the distinct name Tanach (and Tanachites), corresponding to Hebrew Tahan (and Tahanites).
notes.26:40: Greek reads the distinct name Eden (and Edenites), corresponding to Hebrew Eran (and Eranites).
notes.26:42: Greek reads the distinct names Asyber (and Asyberites) and Jachiran (and Jachiranites), corresponding to Hebrew Ashbel and Ahiram.
notes.26:43: Greek lists only Sophan (and Sophanites), corresponding to Hebrew Shephupham while omitting Hupham.
notes.26:44: Greek reads Adar and Naamani (corresponding to Hebrew Ard and Naaman) and omits their clan formulas.
notes.26:45: Greek gives Benjamin's census total as 35,500, whereas the Hebrew reads 45,600.
notes.26:46: Greek reads the distinct name Sami (and Samites), corresponding to Hebrew Shuham (and Shuhamites).
notes.26:47: Greek gives Dan's census total as 64,600 (using the Greek alphabetic numeral chi for 600), whereas the Hebrew reads 64,400.
notes.26:48: Greek reads the distinct name Sael (and Saelites), corresponding to Hebrew Jahzeel (and Jahzeelites).
notes.26:50: Greek gives Naphtali's census total as 30,300, whereas the Hebrew reads 45,400.
notes.26:58: Greek lists four Levitical clans (omitting the Mahlites of the Hebrew) and places the clan of Korah before the Mushites.
notes.26:59: Greek literally reads "who bore these to Levi in Egypt," whereas the Hebrew reads "who was born to Levi in Egypt."
notes.26:65: Greek reads singular "to him" (referring to Moses), whereas the Hebrew reads plural "of them."
notes.27:3: The Greek text combines MT verses 3 and 4 into a single verse and frames the request as a third-person imperative prohibition ("Let the name of our father not be blotted out") rather than the Hebrew rhetorical question ("Why should the name of our father be withdrawn?").
notes.27:12: Instead of transliterating Hebrew Abarim, the Greek renders it geographically as "the mountain on the other side" and explicitly identifies it as "this Mount Nebo" (compare Deut 32:49), while also adding "of Canaan" and "as a possession."
notes.27:14: Rather than transliterating Hebrew Meribah, the Greek translates it as "water of contention" and adds the explicit clause "you did not sanctify Me at the water before them."
notes.27:21: The Greek renders Hebrew Urim etymologically as "the Manifestations" (Greek ton delon) and uses a plural verb ("they shall inquire of him") where the Hebrew has singular ("he shall inquire for him").
notes.28:2: Where the Hebrew text speaks of "My food ... at its appointed time," the Greek reads "My offerings ... at My feasts."
notes.28:5: Throughout chapter 28, Greek thysia ("sacrifice") designates the flour offering corresponding to the Hebrew grain offering (minchah), while karpoma ("fire-offering") designates an offering burned on the altar.
notes.28:26: Instead of a term for "firstfruits," the Greek reads "the day of the new produce" (literally "of the new things"), paralleling "a new sacrifice" in the same verse.
notes.28:31: The Greek verse boundary splits "the whole burnt offering | that is perpetual" across 28:30-31, and 28:31 specifies "their sacrifice for Me" where the Hebrew reads "its grain offering."
notes.29:1: Greek hemera semasias ("day of signaling") refers to the sounding of trumpet signals, corresponding to the Hebrew Festival of Trumpets (teruah).
notes.29:3: In Septuagint Numbers, Greek thysia ("sacrifice") is the regular term for the accompanying grain offering (Hebrew minchah), here specified as fine flour mixed with oil.
notes.29:32: Unlike the other days of the festival (vv. 17, 20, 23, 26, 29), the Greek text omits "without blemish" (amomous) here.
notes.29:35: Greek exodion ("closing festival") denotes the concluding observance at the end of the seven-day feast, corresponding to the Hebrew "solemn assembly" (atseret).
notes.29:39: Greek soteria ("deliverance offerings") is the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew peace or fellowship offerings (shelamim).
notes.30:1: Following Septuagint and Hebrew versification, chapter 30 begins here (29:40 in an alternative versification), shifting the chapter's verse numbers ahead by one.
notes.30:6: Greek kathariei ("will cleanse," also in vv. 9, 13) declares the woman clear of guilt, where the Hebrew text reads "will forgive."
notes.30:7: Greek kata ten diastolen ton cheileon autes ("according to the utterance of her lips") links to the vows as a qualifying phrase rather than the Hebrew alternative "or the rash utterance of her lips."
notes.30:13: Greek periaireo (literally "remove" or "take away," also in vv. 14, 16) denotes canceling or annulling the binding force of a vow.
notes.30:16: The Greek text reads "his sin" (ten hamartian autou), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "her iniquity."
notes.31:6: The Greek repeats 'a thousand from a tribe,' adds 'son of Aaron,' and reads plural 'in their hands' where the Hebrew MT reads singular 'in his hand.'
notes.31:12: The Greek transliterates Hebrew 'arboth' ('plains') as the proper place-name 'Araboth of Moab,' and reads 'all the sons of Israel' where the Hebrew MT has 'the congregation of the sons of Israel.'
notes.31:17: Greek 'apartia' literally means movable household goods or baggage, used here and in v. 18 (like 'aposkeue' in v. 9) to designate dependents or children.
notes.31:22: Greek 'plen' ('besides, apart from') with the genitive renders Hebrew 'ak' ('only') and reverses the order of the last two metals to 'lead and tin'; v. 23 then condenses the clause to 'every item shall pass through fire.'
notes.31:36: The Greek reads 335,500 ('five thousand' rather than 'seven thousand'), whereas v. 43 and the Hebrew MT read 337,500 (matching the tribute of 675 in v. 37).
notes.32:9: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Eshcol ("cluster") literally as "Valley of the Cluster" (Φάραγγα βότρυος).
notes.32:12: The Greek renders the Hebrew gentilic "the Kenizzite" as ὁ διακεχωρισμένος ("the one set apart") and uses the singular verb συνεπηκολούθησεν ("he followed closely"), following v. 11 where it also includes the Septuagint plus "who know evil and good" and reads third-person "which He swore" before "after Me."
notes.32:23: The Greek reads "you will know your sin when evils overtake you" (ὅταν ὑμᾶς καταλάβῃ τὰ κακά), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "know that your sin will find you out."
notes.32:30: The Greek includes the substantial directive "for the war before the Lord, bring their dependents, their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan," absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text (here and throughout the chapter ἀποσκευή denotes non-combatant dependents and household belongings). In v. 31, the Greek also reads arthrous ὁ κύριος ("our lord," referring to Moses as in vv. 25 and 27) rather than the Hebrew divine name.
notes.32:35: The Greek reads "Sophar" (Σωφάρ, lacking the element "Atroth-" of Hebrew Atroth-shophan) and renders the Hebrew place name Jogbehah as the verb phrase "and they raised them up" (καὶ ὕψωσαν αὐτάς). Similarly, v. 36 reads "Namram" (Ναμράμ) without "Beth-," and v. 38 omits Nebo while describing the cities as "encircled" (περικεκυκλωμένας).
notes.32:42: The Greek preserves the distinct proper names Nabau (Νάβαυ), Kaath (Καάθ), and Naboth (Νάβωθ) with the plural pronoun "them" (αὐτάς), corresponding to Nobah, Kenath, and Nobah ("it") in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.33:6: The Greek itinerary preserves several Septuagint-distinct place names and literal translations where the Hebrew differs, including Buthan (vv. 6-7, Hebrew Etham), the mouth of Epiroth and Hiroth (vv. 7-8, Pi-hahiroth), Bitterness (vv. 8-9, Marah), Raphaka (vv. 12-13, Dophkah), Elim repeated here instead of Hebrew Alush (vv. 13-14), and Graves of Craving (vv. 16-17, Kibroth-hattaavah).
notes.33:20: Several wilderness station names in vv. 20-35 follow distinct Septuagint forms rather than the Masoretic Hebrew: Lemona (Libnah), Dessa (Rissah), Makellath (Kehelathah), Shepher without Mount (Mount Shepher), Kataath (Tahath), Tarath (Terah), Zalmonah repeated from vv. 41-42 (Hashmonah), Banaia (Bene-jaakan), Mount Gadgad (Hor-haggidgad), Setebatha (Jotbathah), and Sebrona (Abronah).
notes.33:36: Unlike the Hebrew, which identifies the wilderness of Zin directly with Kadesh, the Septuagint adds an extra stage from the wilderness of Zin to the wilderness of Paran (Kadesh); in v. 38 it omits Mount Hor, and in v. 40 it omits in the Negev while leaving heard as a suspended participle.
notes.33:48: The Septuagint renders Hebrew plains of Moab as west of Moab (vv. 48-50, connecting Hebrew araboth with evening/west) and preserves distinct final station forms: Soboth (vv. 43-44, Oboth), Gai on the other side (vv. 44-45, Iye-abarim), and between Aesimoth as far as Belsa (v. 49, from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim).
notes.33:52: In the closing command (vv. 52-55), the Septuagint translates Hebrew drive out/dispossess as destroy, figured stones as watchtowers, high places as pillars, the lot as his name (v. 54, along with their tribes instead of your clans), and thorns in your sides as darts in your sides (v. 55).
notes.34:4: The Greek reads Ennak (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Zin) and translates Hazar-addar as "the village of Arad" (epaulin Arad).
notes.34:7: Greek to oros to oros ("the mountain, the mountain," repeated in v. 8) renders the Hebrew place name Hor ha-har ("Mount Hor") literally as a doubled common noun.
notes.34:11: In vv. 8-11 the Greek preserves several distinctive place names and renderings: Saradak (MT Zedad), Dephrona (MT Ziphron), Harsenaim/Harsenain (MT Hazar-enan), Sepphamar (MT Shepham), Bela (MT Riblah, repeated in the second clause), "springs" (MT Ain), and Chenara (MT Chinnereth).
notes.34:15: The Greek reads "from the south toward the east" (apo notou kat' anatolas), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "eastward toward the sunrise."
notes.34:20: Throughout vv. 20-28 the Greek preserves distinctive forms for several tribal leaders and fathers compared to the Hebrew Masoretic Text: Salamiel son of Semiud (v. 20; MT Shemuel son of Ammihud), Eldad (v. 21; MT Elidad), Bakchir son of Egli (v. 22; MT Bukki son of Jogli), Suphi (v. 23; MT Ephod), Sabatha (v. 24; MT Shiphtan), Oza (v. 26; MT Azzan), Achior (v. 27; MT Ahihud), and Beniamiud (v. 28; MT Ammihud).
notes.35:1: Greek epi dysmon Moab ("at the west of Moab") reflects interpreting Hebrew arbot ("plains") in connection with ereb ("west/sunset").
notes.35:4: The Greek specifies "two thousand cubits" here (matching v. 5), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "one thousand cubits" in v. 4.
notes.35:21: The Greek repeats the capital sentence ("the killer must surely be put to death") after "he is a murderer," an expansion absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.35:32: Greek tou phygein ("for fleeing") renders the Hebrew verb as an infinitive rather than a participle ("for one who has fled"), and specifies "the high priest" where the Hebrew has "the priest."
notes.35:33: Greek phonoktoneo ("stain with murder") is a rare compound verb used here to emphasize pollution specifically through bloodshed, distinct from miaino ("defile") in v. 34.
notes.36:1: The Septuagint uniquely includes "and before Eleazar the priest," which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text (cf. Num 27:2), and refers to the Gileadite group as a "tribe" rather than a clan.
notes.36:4: Greek aphesis ("release") is the Septuagint's regular term for the Hebrew Jubilee (cf. Lev 25:10).
notes.36:5: Greek houtos ("Thus") renders Hebrew ken with its sense "so/thus" rather than "rightly" (contrast Num 27:6, where the Septuagint renders ken as orthos, "rightly").
notes.36:11: The Septuagint orders the five daughters of Zelophehad with Mahlah last rather than first as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, and uses the idiom "became to their cousins" (i.e., "were married to their cousins") without an explicit word for "wives."
notes.36:13: The Septuagint includes "the statutes" alongside commandments and judgments, omits "to the sons of Israel," and renders Hebrew arbot ("plains") as "the west" (lit. "sunsets") of Moab.

unplaced.text: And they shall put My name upon the sons of Israel, and I, the Lord, will bless them."
unplaced.note: In the Saints Greek Critical Text this verse follows the blessing (vv. 24-26); it has no separate place in the Saints.Bible numbering, so it is shown after 6:26.
